html:
The terms used in this workstation and in Logix Designer, A to Z, as the page’s own glossary has them.

A
Accumulator (.ACC)
The running value of a timer (milliseconds elapsed) or a counter (counts so far). It is a DINT, so it shows up for compare and math instructions, not for XIC.
Adapter
The EtherNet/IP device that is owned and answers the scanner: a camera, a drive, a rack of remote I/O.
Add-On Instruction (AOI)
An instruction you define yourself: parameters, local tags and a ladder routine, packaged under one name and used like TON or MOV. Every call needs its own backing tag. See the Add-On Instructions section.
Alias tag
A second name for another tag or an I/O point. Start_PB aliased to Local:1:I.Data.0 is that input, under a readable name. Cross Reference treats the alias and its target as the same thing.
Analog I/O
A channel that carries a number instead of on/off: a level, a weight, a speed reference. Here it is an INT on the 1769-IF4 and 1769-OF4 cards.
Array
A tag with a Dim: Name[0] to Name[Dim-1], all of one data type. Used by the file, shift, FIFO and sequencer instructions.
Assemble (edits)
The last step of an online edit: the accepted edits become the program and the original rungs are removed.
Assembly (CIP)
A block of bytes an EtherNet/IP device exposes as one object, class 4. The input assembly is what the device produces, the output assembly is what it consumes. The EDS file gives the instance numbers and sizes.
B
Backing tag
The tag of an Add-On Instruction's own data type that goes with one call. It holds that call's parameters and local tags, so two calls with two backing tags run independently.
Backplane
The bus the controller and its local cards sit on. Local:3:O.Data.0 means slot 3 on the backplane.
Base tag
The real tag or I/O address behind an alias.
BOOL
One bit: 0 or 1. What XIC, XIO and OTE work on.
Branch
A parallel path in a rung, written [ leg , leg ]. Power gets through if any leg is true.
Bridge
The small server (TcpBridge, built into LogixConnect.exe) that gives the page real TCP and UDP sockets. Everything that talks to hardware goes through it.
Bumpless transfer
Switching a PID loop between manual and automatic without a jump in the output.
C
Carousel feeder
A turntable carrying magazines of parts round to a feed station, so one machine can run from many magazines: when the one at the station is empty the turntable indexes the next full one round. On the inspection line, 20 magazines of 200 cards feed the transport track.
CIP
Common Industrial Protocol: the object model (classes, instances, attributes, services) that EtherNet/IP carries.
Class 1 connection
A cyclic I/O connection: after a Forward Open, both ends send their data over UDP 2222 every RPI. Also called implicit messaging.
CompactLogix
The Allen-Bradley controller family this workstation is modelled on (1769-L33ER).
Consumed tag
A controller tag whose value is read from another controller at a fixed interval (RPI).
Continuous task
The task that runs over and over as fast as it can. Here MainTask scans every 20 ms.
CONTROL
The structure the file instructions use to keep their place: .LEN, .POS and the status bits .EN .DN .ER .EM .UL.
Control variable (CV)
The output a control loop moves: a valve position, a heater power, a speed reference.
Controller Organizer
The tree on the left: controller tags, tasks, programs and routines, Add-On Instructions, data types, I/O configuration.
Controller tags
Tags every program can use. All I/O and alias tags are controller tags. Program tags belong to one program.
Counter
CTU and CTD count rung transitions into .ACC and set .DN when .ACC reaches .PRE. RES clears it.
Cross Reference
A list of every instruction that reads or writes a tag, across all routines, with the ones that write it marked Destructive. Ctrl+E.
D
Data context
Which call of an Add-On Instruction you are looking at when its logic is open: the definition, or one backing tag's live values.
Data type
What a tag holds: BOOL, SINT, INT, DINT, REAL, STRING, a structure such as TIMER, a user-defined type or an Add-On Instruction's type.
Deadband
A range around the setpoint inside which the error is treated as zero, so the output does not chase noise.
Destructive reference
A place where an instruction writes a tag (OTE, MOV destination, a timer instruction on its timer). Cross Reference marks these with Y.
Destructive reference
An instruction that writes the tag (OTE, MOV destination, TON on its timer) rather than only reading it. Two destructive references to one bit is the classic double-coil bug.
DINT
A 32-bit signed integer. The default number type in Logix.
Done bit (.DN)
Set by a timer when .ACC reaches .PRE, by a counter when the count is reached, by a message when it completes.
E
EDS file
Electronic Data Sheet: the text file a vendor ships that describes an EtherNet/IP device. The identity, the assemblies, the connections and their sizes come from it.
Enable bit (.EN)
True while the instruction's rung-in condition is true (timers, messages, file instructions).
EnableIn / EnableOut
The two built-in parameters of every Add-On Instruction: the rung-in condition it was called with, and the rung-out condition it passes on.
EtherNet/IP
CIP carried over standard Ethernet: explicit messages on TCP 44818 and cyclic I/O on UDP 2222.
Event task
A task that runs when something happens: an EVENT instruction, a trigger tag going true or changing, or a timeout with no trigger.
Exclusive owner
The one scanner allowed to write a device's outputs. A second one is refused with an ownership conflict.
Explicit messaging
Request and reply, one at a time, on TCP: read this attribute, write that tag. The MSG instruction does this.
Expression
A formula written out, as in CPT, CMP, FAL, FSC and Structured Text: Level > 50 AND NOT Fault, or Src[C.POS] * 2 + 1.
F
Fault handler
A program under Controller Fault Handler that runs when a major fault happens. Here it runs once and the fault is cleared.
Fault, major
An error that stops the controller: mode shows Faulted and logic stops until Clear Faults, unless a fault handler program clears it. Integer divide by zero is one.
Fault, minor
An error that is logged while the scan carries on, such as arithmetic overflow.
FBD_TIMER, FBD_COUNTER, FBD_ONESHOT
The structures the Structured Text timers, counter and one-shots work on (TONR, TOFR, RTOR, CTUD, OSRI, OSFI). You set their inputs, such as .TimerEnable and .PRE, then call the instruction.
FIFO
First in, first out: FFL loads a value into an array, FFU unloads the oldest one.
File instruction
An instruction that works through an array one element at a time using a CONTROL tag: FAL, FSC, AVE, SRT, STD, COP, FLL.
Force
An override on an I/O point from the programming software, on top of the device (inputs) or the logic (outputs). Forces act only while enabled.
Forward Open
The CIP request that opens a connection. The scanner asks for sizes and an RPI, the device answers with the connection IDs, then cyclic data starts.
FreqCommand / OutputFreq
A drive's speed reference and its actual output frequency, in hundredths of a hertz: 6000 is 60.00 Hz.
G
GSV / SSV
Get / Set System Value: read or write controller data such as the wall clock, task scan times or a module's EntryStatus.
I
I/O Configuration
The part of the organizer listing the local cards and the Ethernet modules the controller owns.
I/O Monitor
The live list of every input and output point with its value, the device wired to it and the rungs that use it.
Implicit messaging
Cyclic I/O data with no request: both ends just send at the RPI. See Class 1 connection.
In-Sight
Cognex's vision system family. Over EtherNet/IP it exposes trigger and status bits and an inspection results area.
Index pulse
A short input once a pitch, at a fixed point of the card's travel, used to clock a shift register (BSL) so each card's result moves with it. On the inspection line it comes 0.85 of a pitch past the camera, after the result is in.
Indirect addressing
Choosing an array element with a tag instead of a number: Recipe[Step]. The element is picked each time the instruction runs. A subscript outside the array is a major fault.
Inhibit
Configured but switched off: an inhibited task or module stays in the project and does not run.
Input / Output / InOut (parameter)
How an Add-On Instruction parameter is passed. Input: the value is copied in. Output: the value is copied out. InOut: the logic works on the caller's tag directly.
Instruction
One element of a rung: a contact, a coil or a box such as TON, MOV or an Add-On Instruction.
INT
A 16-bit signed integer.
Interlock
A condition in series that must be true before an output may come on.
J
JSR / SBR / RET
Jump To Subroutine, and the Subroutine and Return instructions that receive and hand back its parameters.
L
L5X
The XML file Studio 5000 uses to export and import a project or a piece of one. File → Import L5X and Export L5X read and write it.
Ladder Diagram (LD)
The relay-style language of rungs between two power rails. The only language here.
Latch / Unlatch
OTL sets a bit and it stays set until OTU clears it, whatever the rungs do in between.
LIFO
Last in, first out: LFL loads a value into an array, LFU unloads the newest one.
Listen-only
A connection that receives a device's inputs without owning its outputs. In-Sight cameras do not offer one.
Local tag
A tag that belongs to an Add-On Instruction and exists once per backing tag: its timers, counters and working values.
M
Main routine
The routine a program runs each scan. Other routines run only when a JSR calls them.
MCR zone
The rungs between two MCR instructions. While the first MCR rung is false, every rung in the zone is scanned as false, so ordinary outputs drop. It is not a substitute for a hard-wired safety relay.
Module
A device in the I/O configuration: a local card, or an EtherNet/IP device created from an EDS file.
MSG
The Message instruction: one explicit request to a device or another controller, with .EN .DN .ER status bits.
N
Neutral text
The text form of a rung, for example XIC(Start)OTE(Motor); . Press Enter on a rung to edit it this way.
No-test mask
The last eight bytes of a recipe string, laid out like the row bytes: a well whose bit is 1 is not inspected, whatever it holds.
O
One-shot
ONS, OSR, OSF: true for exactly one scan when the rung goes true (or false), so something happens once per event.
Online
Connected to the controller, so you see live values. Here the workstation is always online with its own controller unless you go offline.
Online edit
Changing logic while the controller runs. The change is pending (i), then accepted (I), then tested, then assembled. See the Online edits section.
Operand
A value or tag an instruction works on: the bit of an XIC, the source and destination of a MOV.
OTE
Output Energize: the coil. The bit follows the rung, every scan.
Overlap
A task triggered again before its previous run had started or finished. Counted in GSV(Task,name,OverlapCount).
Ownership conflict
The error a device returns when a second scanner asks for a connection it has already given to another.
P
Pen
One tag plotted on a trend. A trend holds up to 8, each with its own colour.
Pending edit
An online edit that is still only in the editor: the i rung. The controller has not been given it yet.
Periodic task
A task that runs at a fixed period in milliseconds, for logic that must run at a known rate.
PID
Proportional, Integral, Derivative: the standard closed-loop control instruction. It compares the process variable with the setpoint and moves the control variable to close the gap.
PLC
Programmable Logic Controller: the industrial computer that reads inputs, runs the logic and writes outputs, over and over.
Power flow
Whether the rung is true up to a given point. The green highlighting on contacts and wires.
Pre-emption
A higher-priority task interrupting a lower one part-way through. Here it happens between rungs; the interrupted task then carries on from where it stopped.
Preset (.PRE)
The target of a timer (milliseconds) or counter (counts).
Priority (task)
1 is highest, 15 lowest. Periodic and event tasks all outrank the continuous task.
Process variable (PV)
The measured value a control loop is controlling: a level, a temperature, a speed.
Produced / consumed tag
A tag one controller broadcasts and another receives cyclically. Not supported here.
Produced tag
A controller tag that is sent to another controller at a fixed interval (RPI).
Program
A group of routines with its own tags, scheduled in a task.
Program mode
Controller mode where inputs update but no logic runs and outputs are off.
Program tags (local tags)
Tags that belong to one program, listed under Parameters and Local Tags. Only that program's routines can use them, and inside that program they win over a controller tag of the same name.
Q
Quick Watch
Your own list of tags with live values that you can change, shown in a floating window (Alt+3) and in the Watch tab of the output window. Saved with the project.
R
REAL
A 32-bit floating-point number.
Recipe string (card)
The product's line in the product table: 1,NAME,64, then eight row bytes (a byte a row of the 8 × 8 card, the 128 bit being column 1), then eight no-test bytes. Sent in rows; the camera inspects in columns: well = (column − 1) × 8 + row.
Remote controller
Another controller this one shares produced and consumed tags with: simulated inside the project, or a real one reached through the bridge.
Remote I/O
Inputs and outputs on a block out on the network instead of in the controller chassis. Their tags are named after the module, such as RIO1:I.Pt00.
Requested Packet Interval (RPI)
How often, in milliseconds, each end of a cyclic connection sends its data.
Retentive
Keeps its value when the rung goes false. RTO is a retentive timer; only RES clears it.
Rodless cylinder
A pneumatic cylinder whose piston drives a carriage running along the outside of the tube instead of a rod, so a long stroke takes no more room than the tube. On the inspection line it pushes the empty tray from the lift into the fill position.
Routine
A list of rungs. Each program has a main routine and may have more.
Run mode
Controller mode where logic scans and outputs are driven.
Rung
One line of ladder: conditions on the left, outputs on the right.
Rung comment
Free text above a rung saying what it does. Ctrl+D.
S
Sandbox
The free-form project where you place your own devices and wire them to I/O.
Scan
One pass: read inputs, run the tasks, write outputs. 20 ms here.
Scanner
The EtherNet/IP device that opens connections and owns the adapters: normally the PLC, here the workstation.
Scope
Where a tag lives and who can see it: the controller (everyone) or one program (only its routines). The Scope box in the tag editor switches between them.
Seal-in
A branch around a start contact using the output's own bit, so a momentary start keeps the output on until a stop breaks the rung.
Sequencer
SQO steps through an array of words and copies each to an output through a mask.
Setpoint (SP)
The value a control loop is trying to hold.
SINT
An 8-bit signed integer.
Slot
A position on the backplane. In a route, slot 0 is the CompactLogix controller.
STRING
Text of up to 82 characters with a .LEN and the characters in .DATA.
Structure
A tag made of members: TIMER, COUNTER, CONTROL, MESSAGE, a user-defined type or an Add-On Instruction tag.
Structured Text (ST)
A text language for routines: assignments with :=, IF, CASE, FOR, WHILE and REPEAT. Good for math, loops and decisions that are clumsy in ladder. See the Structured Text section.
T
Tag
A named piece of controller memory. Logix addresses everything by tag name.
Task
What schedules programs: continuous, periodic or event. Each has a priority; a higher-priority task interrupts a lower one.
TCP Client Socket
A sandbox device that opens a plain TCP connection through the bridge to send and receive text, for equipment that speaks ASCII.
Test (edits)
Running the accepted edits in place of the original rungs without committing to them. Untest goes back.
Test mode
Controller mode where logic scans but outputs stay off.
Timer
TON, TOF, RTO: time a condition in milliseconds into .ACC and set .DN at .PRE. .TT is true while timing.
Timing bit (.TT)
True while a timer is counting: enabled and not done yet.
Transfer platen
A square plate on a carriage under a beam, with grippers at its corners, that picks a tray up (from the top of a tray lift, say), carries it along the beam and sets it down in a nest. On the inspection line it brings each empty tray over behind the full one going out; TT_Go runs it, TT_Grip closes the grippers, TT_AtStack, TT_AtNest and TT_Gripped say where it is and what it holds.
Trap-door reject gate
A section of the conveyor that drops open under a failed card so it falls into the bin below, instead of a pusher sweeping it off.
Tray indexer (pawl indexer)
A cylinder each end of a tray that lifts a pawl behind the tray's trailing rail and strokes it one row forward, then drops the pawl and runs back a row for the next stroke. Run right through, the pawls push the full tray out onto the conveyor. On the inspection line: Idx_Lift (pawls up), Idx_Step (a row), Idx_Out (the tray out); Idx_Home, Idx_Up, Idx_Ext, Idx_AtOut say where it is.
Tray lift (tray destacker)
A lift that holds a stack of empty trays and raises the top one to a transfer level, a tray pitch at a time, so a transfer can take it into the machine.
Trend
A chart of tag values against controller time. Each plotted tag is a pen. See the Trends section.
Trigger
The signal that makes a camera acquire an image. Over EtherNet/IP: set Trigger Enable, pulse Trigger, wait for the acknowledge and Results Valid.
U
UCMM
Unconnected Message Manager: explicit messages sent without opening a connection first.
UID / UIE
User Interrupt Disable and Enable. Rungs between them cannot be interrupted by another task.
User-Defined Data Type (UDT)
A structure you define: named members of any type. A tag of that type gets Tag.Member for each.
V
Variable frequency drive (VFD)
A drive that runs an AC motor at a commanded frequency. The built-in one uses the PowerFlex 525 tags: Start, Stop, FreqCommand out; Ready, Active, Faulted, OutputFreq in.
Verify
Check every rung for errors without running anything. The results are in the Errors window.
W
Watchdog
The limit on how long a task may run. Here a loop that never ends is stopped with a major fault (type 6) instead of freezing the controller.
X
XIC
Examine If Closed: a contact that is true when the bit is 1.
XIO
Examine If Open: a contact that is true when the bit is 0.
Z
Zone markers (i I r R d D)
The letters in the rung margin during an online edit. Lower case is pending, upper case is in the controller: i/I the new rung, r/R the original it replaces, d/D a rung being deleted.
